\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter04.RandomRestrictions}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Random subset weight]
\lean{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b003}
\label{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, a real parameter $\delta$, and a subset $J$ of
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, define its weight to be $\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegative random subset weight]
\lean{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight_nonneg}
\label{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\delta\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $0\le\delta\le1$, and let
$J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Then $\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}\ge0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total weight of random subsets]
\lean{FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
\label{FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
\difficulty{4}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every real number $\\delta$, the sum over all
subsets $J$ of $\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$ of $\\delta^{|J|}(1-\\delta)^{n-|J|}$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Weighted subset sum]
\lean{FABL.expectDeltaRandomSubset}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b003}
\label{FABL.expectDeltaRandomSubset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
For a natural number $n$, a real parameter $\delta$, and a real-valued function $g$ on
subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, define its weighted sum to be
$\sum_{J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}g(J)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Expected value over random restrictions]
\lean{FABL.expectRandomRestriction}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p005-b001}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{
  pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b001,
  pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b003
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b003}
\label{FABL.expectRandomRestriction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
For a natural number $n$, a real parameter $\delta$, and a real-valued function $g$ that
assigns a value to each subset $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and each sign assignment $z$
on its complement, define the expected value over random restrictions as
$\sum_{J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}\,\mathbb{E}_{z}[g(J,z)]$,
where the expectation is over sign assignments on the complement of $J$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Extension under a fixed restriction]
\lean{FABL.extendedSignRestriction}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p075-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b004
}
\label{FABL.extendedSignRestriction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.combineSignCube}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ map sign vectors on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ to a type
$\alpha$, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and fix a sign assignment $z$ on the
complement of $J$. The extension of $f$ associated with $J$ and $z$ maps each sign
vector $x$ to the value of $f$ at the sign vector that agrees with $x$ on $J$ and with
$z$ outside $J$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation of an extended sign restriction]
\lean{FABL.extendedSignRestriction_apply}
\label{FABL.extendedSignRestriction_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.extendedSignRestriction}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $J$ be a set of coordinates among the $n$
coordinates, and let $z$ assign signs to the coordinates outside $J$. For any function
$f$ on the sign cube and any sign vector $x$, the extended restriction evaluated at $x$
equals $f$ evaluated at the sign vector formed using $x$ on $J$ and $z$ outside $J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Invariance outside the free coordinates]
\lean{FABL.extendedSignRestriction_setCoordinate_of_not_mem}
\label{FABL.extendedSignRestriction_setCoordinate_of_not_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.Sign, FABL.combineSignCube_apply_fixed, FABL.combineSignCube_apply_free, FABL.extendedSignRestriction, FABL.setCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $f$ map sign
vectors of length $n$ to a set $\alpha$. Fix signs on the coordinates outside $J$, and
form a new sign vector by taking its coordinates in $J$ from the input and its other
coordinates from those fixed signs. Changing an input coordinate $i\notin J$ to either
sign $b\in\{\pm1\}$ leaves the value of this restricted function unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing derivative outside the free coordinates]
\lean{FABL.discreteDerivative_extendedSignRestriction_of_not_mem}
\label{FABL.discreteDerivative_extendedSignRestriction_of_not_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.extendedSignRestriction, FABL.extendedSignRestriction_setCoordinate_of_not_mem, FABL.setCoordinate}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and fix signs on all coordinates outside
$J$. If $i\notin J$, then the discrete derivative in coordinate $i$ of the function
obtained by extending this restriction is identically zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Influence outside the restricted coordinates]
\lean{FABL.influence_extendedSignRestriction_of_not_mem}
\label{FABL.influence_extendedSignRestriction_of_not_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.discreteDerivative_extendedSignRestriction_of_not_mem, FABL.extendedSignRestriction, FABL.influence}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and fix signs on all
coordinates outside $J$. For the function obtained by allowing the coordinates in $J$ to
vary freely while using those fixed signs elsewhere, every coordinate $i\notin J$ has
influence zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate restriction types]
\lean{FABL.CoordRestriction}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p005-b001}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p075-b002}
\label{FABL.CoordRestriction}
\leanok
A coordinate restriction has exactly three possible types: free, fixed to $1$, or fixed
to $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate restriction weights]
\lean{FABL.coordRestrictionWeight}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p084-b002}
\label{FABL.coordRestrictionWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction}
Assign weight $1/2$ to a free coordinate restriction and weight $1/4$ to each of the
restrictions fixing the coordinate to $1$ or to $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Total weight of one-coordinate restrictions]
\lean{FABL.sum_coordRestrictionWeight}
\label{FABL.sum_coordRestrictionWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.coordRestrictionWeight}
\difficulty{4}
The three coordinate restrictions—free, fixed to $1$, or fixed to $-1$—have weights
$1/2$, $1/4$, and $1/4$, respectively, and their weights sum to $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegative restriction weights]
\lean{FABL.coordRestrictionWeight_nonneg}
\label{FABL.coordRestrictionWeight_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.coordRestrictionWeight}
\difficulty{4}
The weight of every coordinate restriction is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restriction assignment weight]
\lean{FABL.restrictionAssignmentWeight}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p005-b001}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b003}
\label{FABL.restrictionAssignmentWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.coordRestrictionWeight}
For a natural number $n$ and an assignment $\rho$ of a coordinate restriction to each
index in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, define its weight as the product over all indices of the
weight of the restriction assigned there.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of assignment weight]
\lean{FABL.restrictionAssignmentWeight_nonneg}
\label{FABL.restrictionAssignmentWeight_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.coordRestrictionWeight_nonneg, FABL.restrictionAssignmentWeight}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and assign to each of the $n$ coordinates one of the states
“free,” “fixed to $1$,” or “fixed to $-1$.” The product of the coordinate weights, which
are $rac12$ for a free state and $rac14$ for either fixed state, is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total weight of restriction assignments]
\lean{FABL.sum_restrictionAssignmentWeight}
\label{FABL.sum_restrictionAssignmentWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.coordRestrictionWeight, FABL.restrictionAssignmentWeight, FABL.sum_coordRestrictionWeight}
\difficulty{3}
For any nonnegative integer $n$, assign independently to each of the $n$ coordinates one
of three restrictions: leave it free, fix it to $1$, or fix it to $-1$. Give these
choices respective weights $1/2$, $1/4$, and $1/4$, and give an assignment the product
of its coordinate weights. The sum of the weights of all restriction assignments is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Falsification of a literal]
\lean{FABL.Literal.isFalsified}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004}
\label{FABL.Literal.isFalsified}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.Literal, FABL.Sign}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let a literal specify a coordinate $i\\in\\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
and a required sign $s\\in\\{\\pm1\\}$, and let $\\rho$ assign each coordinate either no
restriction or a fixed sign. The literal is falsified exactly when its coordinate is
fixed to a sign different from $s$; a free coordinate does not falsify it.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Restricted width of a term]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.restrictedWidthOf}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b005
}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.restrictedWidthOf}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal.isFalsified}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a conjunction of literals with pairwise distinct
coordinates, and let $\\rho$ assign each coordinate either no restriction or a fixed
sign. If any literal is falsified by $\\rho$, define the restricted width of $T$ to be
$0$; otherwise, it is the number of literals whose coordinates are unrestricted.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Restricted width is bounded by term width]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.restrictedWidthOf_le_width}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.restrictedWidthOf_le_width}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.restrictedWidthOf, FABL.DNFTerm.width}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a DNF term on $n$ coordinates and let each coordinate be free, fixed to $1$,
or fixed to $-1$. The restricted width of $T$ is at most its width, the number of
literals in $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Term not falsified]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b006
}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.Literal.isFalsified}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a conjunction of literals with pairwise distinct
coordinates, and let $\\rho$ assign each coordinate either no restriction or a fixed
sign. The term is not falsified when none of its literals is falsified by $\\rho$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of a nonfalsified term]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified_iff}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified, FABL.Literal.isFalsified}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a DNF term on $n$ coordinates, and assign each
coordinate one of the restrictions free, fixed to $1$, or fixed to $-1$. The indicator
that $T$ is not falsified by this assignment equals true exactly when every literal in
$T$ is not falsified by it.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Positive restricted width prevents falsification]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.restrictedWidthOf_ge_implies_notFalsified}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.restrictedWidthOf_ge_implies_notFalsified}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified, FABL.DNFTerm.restrictedWidthOf}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a DNF term on $n$ coordinates and let each coordinate be free, fixed to $1$,
or fixed to $-1$. If a positive integer $w$ is at most the restricted width of $T$ under
this restriction, then no literal of $T$ is falsified by the restriction.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $\delta\in\mathbb
R$. The average over random coordinate restrictions, with each subset
$J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ weighted by $\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}$ and the signs
outside $J$ chosen uniformly, of the empty-set Fourier coefficient of the restricted
function equals the empty-set Fourier coefficient of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total weight of supersets]
\lean{FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight_supset}
\label{FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight_supset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $b4$ be a real number, and let $S$ be a subset of
$bbrange{n}=bbrange{n}$ (the indices $0,bbrdots,n-1$). For each subset $J$ of these
indices, assign weight $b4^{|J|}(1-b4)^{n-|J|}$. The sum of the weights over all $J$
containing $S$ is $b4^{|S|}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Ambient restriction Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.ambientRestrictionFourierCoeff}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p006-b004}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p076-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b004
}
\label{FABL.ambientRestrictionFourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube
$\\{\\pm1\\}^n$, let $J,S\\subseteq\\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and let $z$ assign signs to the
coordinates outside $J$. Define the ambient restriction Fourier coefficient at $S$ and
$z$ to be the restriction Fourier coefficient at the free-frequency part of $S$ when
$S\\subseteq J$, and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Ambient restriction coefficient formula]
\lean{FABL.ambientRestrictionFourierCoeff_eq}
\label{FABL.ambientRestrictionFourierCoeff_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.ambientRestrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $J,S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and fix the signs on
the coordinates outside $J$. The ambient restriction Fourier coefficient at $S$ equals
the Fourier coefficient of the restricted function at the part of $S$ lying in $J$ if
$S\subseteq J$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and let
$J,S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Fix the signs outside $J$ and form the Fourier coefficient
of the resulting restricted function at the frequency $S$ when $S\subseteq J$; define
the ambient restriction coefficient to be zero when $S\nsubseteq J$. Its uniform average
over all choices of the fixed signs equals $\widehat f(S)$ if $S\subseteq J$, and equals
zero otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected Fourier coefficient under random restriction]
\lean{FABL.expect_fourierCoeff_randomRestriction}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p006-b004,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p007-b001
}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b001
}
\label{FABL.expect_fourierCoeff_randomRestriction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ambientRestrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight, FABL.expectRandomRestriction, FABL.expect_ambientRestrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight_supset}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $\delta\in\mathbb R$,
and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The average over random coordinate restrictions,
weighted by $\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}$ with the signs outside $J$ chosen
uniformly, of the ambient restriction Fourier coefficient at $S$ equals $\delta^{|S|}$
times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lifting the restricted subset]
\lean{FABL.liftFreeFrequency_freeFrequencyPart_of_subset}
\label{FABL.liftFreeFrequency_freeFrequencyPart_of_subset}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.freeFrequencyPart, FABL.liftFreeFrequency}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $J,S$ be finite subsets of $in n$ such that
$S\subseteq J$. Viewing the elements of $S$ as elements indexed by $J$ and then in $in
n$ recovers exactly $S$.
\end{theorem}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p075-b002}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $J,S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. For each assignment $z$ of signs outside $J$, form the
ambient restriction Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$. Its mean square over uniformly
chosen $z$ is $\sum_{T\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\setminus J}\widehat f\bigl((S\cap J)\cup
T\bigr)^2$ if $S\subseteq J$, and is $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subsets of an intersection]
\lean{FABL.subset_of_inter_eq}
\label{FABL.subset_of_inter_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S,U,J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. If $U\cap J=S$,
then $S\subseteq J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subsets of an intersection]
\lean{FABL.subset_of_inter_eq_left}
\label{FABL.subset_of_inter_eq_left}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $S,U,J\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. If $U\cap J=S$,
then $S\subseteq U$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subset-intersection weight sum]
\lean{FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight_inter_eq}
\label{FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight_inter_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight, FABL.subset_of_inter_eq, FABL.subset_of_inter_eq_left}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\\delta$ be real, and let $S,U$ be subsets of
$\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$. The sum over all subsets $J$ of $\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$ of the weight
$\\delta^{|J|}(1-\\delta)^{n-|J|}$ when $U\\cap J=S$ (and zero otherwise) equals
$\\delta^{|S|}(1-\\delta)^{|U\\setminus S|}$ if $S\\subseteq U$, and equals zero
otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let
$J,S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $S\subseteq J$. For each subset $T$ of the complement
of $J$, form the frequency $S\cup T$. The sum of the squared Fourier coefficients at
these frequencies equals the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients over all
frequencies $U$ whose intersection with $J$ is exactly $S$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $\delta\in\mathbb R$,
and let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The expected square of the ambient restriction
Fourier coefficient at $S$, when each coordinate is independently included in the free
set with weight parameter $\delta$, equals
$\displaystyle\sum_{U\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\mathbf 1_{S\subseteq
U}\,\delta^{|S|}(1-\delta)^{|U\setminus S|}\,\widehat f(U)^2$, where $\widehat f(U)$ is
the uniform Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $U$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weight of subsets containing a coordinate]
\lean{FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight_mem}
\label{FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\\delta$ be real, and let $i$ be a coordinate in
$\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$. The sum over subsets $J$ containing $i$ of
$\\delta^{|J|}(1-\\delta)^{n-|J|}$ is $\\delta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative of an extended sign restriction]
\lean{FABL.discreteDerivative_extendedSignRestriction_of_mem}
\label{FABL.discreteDerivative_extendedSignRestriction_of_mem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.Sign, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.extendedSignRestriction, FABL.setCoordinate, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and fix signs on all coordinates outside
$J$. If $i\in J$, then at every cube point $x$, the discrete derivative in coordinate
$i$ of the function obtained by extending this restriction agrees with the discrete
derivative of $f$ at the point formed from the coordinates of $x$ in $J$ and the fixed
signs outside $J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Free-coordinate restriction]
\lean{FABL.freePart}
\statementsource{arora-barak-ch13-circuit-lowerbounds}{pdf-52929dbaa962-p002-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p075-b002}
\label{FABL.freePart}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FreeSignCube}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J\\subseteq\\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and let
$x\\in\\{\\pm1\\}^n$. The free part of $x$ on $J$ is the assignment on $J$ given by
$j\\mapsto x_j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Free component of the sign cube split]
\lean{FABL.freePart_eq_split}
\label{FABL.freePart_eq_split}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.freePart, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $J$ be a subset of the coordinates $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$,
and let $x$ assign a sign in $\{-1,1\}$ to each coordinate. The restriction of $x$ to
$J$ is the first component of the decomposition of $x$ into its restrictions to $J$ and
to the complement of $J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Squared derivative under coordinate splitting]
\lean{FABL.expect_sq_discreteDerivative_combine}
\label{FABL.expect_sq_discreteDerivative_combine}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.freePart, FABL.freePart_eq_split, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, let
$J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, choose any coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and fix signs
$z$ on the coordinates outside $J$. For a sign vector $x$, combine its restriction to
$J$ with the fixed signs $z$. The mean over uniform $x$ of the square of the discrete
derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ at this combined vector equals the mean of that same
squared derivative over uniform assignments to the coordinates in $J$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product decomposition of derivative influence]
\lean{FABL.expect_sq_discreteDerivative_product}
\label{FABL.expect_sq_discreteDerivative_product}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.FreeSignCube, FABL.combineSignCube, FABL.discreteDerivative, FABL.influence, FABL.signCubeSplitEquiv}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $J$ be any subset of its coordinates, and let $i$ be any coordinate. If
the cube is sampled by choosing signs independently and uniformly on $J$ and on its
complement, then the expected squared discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$
equals the influence of $f$ at $i$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $J\subseteq[n]$, and let $i\in
J$. Averaging over all assignments to the coordinates outside $J$, the influence of the
extended restriction of $f$ to the free coordinates in $J$ at coordinate $i$ equals the
influence of $f$ at $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected influence under extended restriction]
\lean{FABL.expect_influence_extended_randomRestriction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b003
}
\label{FABL.expect_influence_extended_randomRestriction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight, FABL.expectRandomRestriction, FABL.expect_influence_extendedSignRestriction_of_mem, FABL.extendedSignRestriction, FABL.influence, FABL.influence_extendedSignRestriction_of_not_mem, FABL.sum_deltaRandomSubsetWeight_mem}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, let $\delta\in\mathbb R$,
and choose a coordinate $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The average, over random coordinate
restrictions weighted by $\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}$ and uniform signs outside $J$,
of the influence of coordinate $i$ in the extended restricted function equals $\delta$
times the influence of coordinate $i$ in $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total influence under random restrictions]
\lean{FABL.expect_totalInfluence_extended_randomRestriction}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b003
}
\label{FABL.expect_totalInfluence_extended_randomRestriction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.deltaRandomSubsetWeight, FABL.expectRandomRestriction, FABL.expect_influence_extended_randomRestriction, FABL.extendedSignRestriction, FABL.influence, FABL.totalInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $\delta$ be any real number. Choose a subset $J$ of
coordinates with weight $\delta^{|J|}(1-\delta)^{n-|J|}$, and then choose uniformly a
sign assignment $z$ on the coordinates outside $J$; the restriction of $f$ fixes those
coordinates to $z$ and leaves the coordinates in $J$ free. The expectation, with these
weights and uniform choices, of the total influence of this restricted function is
$\delta$ times the total influence of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $\ell$ be a literal on $n$ coordinates. Assign weight $1/2$ to the free restriction
and weight $1/4$ to each of the two restrictions fixing the coordinate to $1$ or $-1$.
The total weight of restrictions under which $\ell$ is not falsified is $3/4$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Local nonfalsification factor]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.localNotFalsifiedFactor}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b006
}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.localNotFalsifiedFactor}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt, FABL.DNFTerm.support, FABL.Literal.isFalsified}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a conjunction of literals with pairwise distinct
coordinates, let $i\\in\\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and let $c$ be a coordinate restriction. If
$i$ is in the support of $T$, the local nonfalsification factor is $0$ when the literal
at $i$ is falsified by the constant restriction $c$, and is $1$ otherwise; if $i$ is
outside the support, the factor is $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Local nonfalsification factor sum]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.localNotFalsifiedFactor_sum}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.localNotFalsifiedFactor_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt, FABL.DNFTerm.localNotFalsifiedFactor, FABL.DNFTerm.support, FABL.Literal.isFalsified, FABL.coordRestrictionWeight, FABL.literal_not_falsified_local_weight, FABL.sum_coordRestrictionWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on $n$ coordinates and $i$ a coordinate. Sum over
the three restriction states, weighting the free state by $1/2$ and each fixed-sign
state by $1/4$, the local factor that is zero when the selected literal at $i$ is
falsified and one otherwise (and is one when $i$ is outside the support). This weighted
sum is $3/4$ if $i$ is in the support of $T$, and $1$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product formula for the nonfalsification indicator]
\lean{FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified_indicator_eq_prod}
\label{FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified_indicator_eq_prod}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_eq, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_index, FABL.DNFTerm.literalAt_mem, FABL.DNFTerm.localNotFalsifiedFactor, FABL.DNFTerm.mem_support_of_mem_literals, FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified, FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified_iff, FABL.DNFTerm.support, FABL.Literal.isFalsified}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a DNF term on $n$ coordinates, and assign each
coordinate one of the restrictions free, fixed to $1$, or fixed to $-1$. The real
indicator of the event that $T$ is not falsified is the product, over all coordinates,
of the local factors that are $0$ when the corresponding literal is falsified and $1$
otherwise; coordinates outside the support contribute $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Weight of nonfalsified terms]
\lean{FABL.term_not_falsified_weight}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b006
}
\label{FABL.term_not_falsified_weight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CoordRestriction, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.card_support, FABL.DNFTerm.localNotFalsifiedFactor, FABL.DNFTerm.localNotFalsifiedFactor_sum, FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified, FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified_indicator_eq_prod, FABL.DNFTerm.support, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.coordRestrictionWeight, FABL.restrictionAssignmentWeight}
\proofstep
  {FABL.𝔽₂}

  {FABL.DNFTerm.notFalsified_indicator_eq_prod}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b005,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b006}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $T$ be a conjunction of literals on distinct
coordinates of the $n$-dimensional sign cube, with width $r$ equal to its number of
literals. Give each coordinate restriction independently weight $1/2$ when free and
$1/4$ for each of the two fixed signs, and let the weight of an assignment be the
product of its coordinate weights. The total weight of assignments under which no
literal of $T$ is falsified is $(3/4)^r$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $T$ be a conjunction of signed literals on $n$
coordinates with pairwise distinct indices, and let $w$ be a natural number. Under the
product distribution on coordinate restrictions that gives probability $1/2$ to leaving
a coordinate free and probability $1/4$ to each of fixing it to $1$ or to $-1$, the
probability that the restricted width of $T$ is at least $w$ is at most $(3/4)^w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Geometric sum over an integer interval]
\lean{FABL.sum_inverse_two_pow_succ_Ico_le}
\label{FABL.sum_inverse_two_pow_succ_Ico_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For all nonnegative integers $m,n$, $\\sum_{k=m}^{n-1}2^{-(k+1)}\\le 2^{-m}$, where the
sum is empty when $n\\le m$.␀
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Selected term of a DNF formula]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.selectedTerm}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b003}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.selectedTerm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFFormula.eval_eq_neg_one_iff, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.empty}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\\varphi$ be a disjunction of conjunctions of
literals, and let $x\\in\\{\\pm1\\}^n$. If $\\varphi(x)=-1$, select a term of $\\varphi$
that evaluates to $-1$ at $x$; if $\\varphi(x)\\ne-1$, select the empty term.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Width of the selected term]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b003}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.width}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\\varphi$ be a disjunction of conjunctions of
literals, and let $x\\in\\{\\pm1\\}^n$. The selected width of $\\varphi$ at $x$ is the
width of the term selected at $x$.
\end{definition}

  {FABL.DNFFormula.selectedTerm}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ coordinates, and
let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. If $\varphi$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$, then the selected term
belongs to the list of terms of $\varphi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Selected term is satisfied]

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p096-b005}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ coordinates, and
let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. If $\varphi$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$, then the selected term of
$\varphi$ evaluates to $-1$ at $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Selected width when the formula evaluates to one]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth_eq_zero_of_eval_ne}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth_eq_zero_of_eval_ne}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedTerm, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ coordinates, and
let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. If $\varphi$ does not evaluate to $-1$ at $x$, then the selected
term has width zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Selected width bounded by dimension]
\lean{FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth_le_dimension}
\label{FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth_le_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedTerm, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth, FABL.DNFTerm.width_le_dimension}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ coordinates, and
let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The width of the selected term is at most $n$.
\end{theorem}

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p093-b004}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on
$\{-1,1\}^n$: each term is a conjunction of literals on distinct coordinates, and the
formula is the disjunction of its terms. At any input $x$, choose a term satisfied by
$x$ if the formula outputs $-1$, and otherwise use the empty term; the number of
coordinates whose flip changes the formula's output, when its output at $x$ is $-1$, is
at most the number of literals in that chosen term.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Selected width tail bound for a DNF]
\lean{FABL.selectedWidth_tail_probability_le}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p100-b001
}
\label{FABL.selectedWidth_tail_probability_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.eval, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedTerm, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedTerm_eval, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedTerm_mem, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth_eq_zero_of_eval_ne, FABL.DNFFormula.size, FABL.DNFTerm, FABL.DNFTerm.eval, FABL.DNFTerm.width, FABL.expect_sum_list_map, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_DNFTerm_eval_neg_one}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form formula on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube, and let $k$ be a positive natural number. For a uniformly
random input $x$, the probability that the selected term of $\varphi$ at $x$ has width
at least $k$ is at most $|\varphi|/2^k$, where $|\varphi|$ is the number of terms in the
formula.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform probability is at most one]
\lean{FABL.uniformProbability_le_one}
\label{FABL.uniformProbability_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, and let $P$ be a predicate on $\Omega$. The
uniform probability that $P$ holds is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expected selected width as a sum of tail probabilities]
\lean{FABL.expect_selectedWidth_eq_sum_tail}
\label{FABL.expect_selectedWidth_eq_sum_tail}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DNFFormula, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth_le_dimension, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on the
$n$-dimensional sign cube, whose terms are conjunctions of literals on distinct
coordinates. For each input $x$, select a term satisfied by $x$ if $\varphi(x)$ is true,
and select the empty term otherwise; let $W(x)$ be the number of literals in the
selected term. The uniform expectation of $W$ over the sign cube equals
$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\Pr[W\ge k+1]$, where the probabilities are uniform on that cube.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\varphi$ be a disjunctive normal form on the sign
cube $\{−1,1\}^n$, and let $s$ be a nonnegative integer such that the number of terms of
$\varphi$ is at most $s$. The uniform expectation over inputs $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$ of the
width of the selected term is at most $\lceil\log_2 s\rceil+1$, where the selected term
is the one chosen when $\varphi(x)=-1$ and is the empty term otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total influence of a bounded-size DNF]
\lean{FABL.totalInfluence_le_two_mul_clog_add_one_of_hasDNFSizeLE}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p095-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p099-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p100-b001
}
\label{FABL.totalInfluence_le_two_mul_clog_add_one_of_hasDNFSizeLE}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.DNFFormula.selectedWidth, FABL.DNFFormula.toBooleanFunction, FABL.HasDNFSizeLE, FABL.IsNegOnePivotal, FABL.card_negOnePivotal_le_selectedWidth, FABL.expect_selectedWidth_le_clog_add_one, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_eq_two_mul_expect_card_negOnePivotal}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$. Suppose there is a
disjunctive normal form formula on $n$ variables with at most $s$ terms that represents
$f$, for some natural number $s$. Then the total influence of the real-valued function
obtained by viewing each output of $f$ as a real number is at most
$2\bigl(\operatorname{clog}_2(s)+1\bigr)$, where $\operatorname{clog}_2(s)$ is the least
natural number $m$ such that $2^m\ge s$.
\end{theorem}
